name: Apprise API
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: A web service and API that sends notifications to over 100 services, such as Discord, Telegram, email and Slack, from saved configurations or one-off requests. It needs a login.
startup: h=$( (python3 --version; cat .apprise-version app/requirements.txt) | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1); if [ "$h" != "$(cat .venv/.raptor-installed 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "Installing Apprise API's Python packages"; rm -rf .venv; python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir --disable-pip-version-check -r app/requirements.txt whitenoise polib && (cd app && ../.venv/bin/python apprise_translations.py >/dev/null) && echo "$h" > .venv/.raptor-installed || exit 1; fi; pw="{{APPRISE_PASSWORD}}"; if [ -z "$pw" ]; then [ -s admin-password.txt ] || (umask 077; head -c 18 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d "\n/+=" > admin-password.txt); pw=$(cat admin-password.txt); echo "Admin password is empty, so the account {{APPRISE_USER}} has the password in admin-password.txt."; fi; export SECRET_KEY="$(cat .secret-key)" APPRISE_PASSWORD="$pw" APPRISE_AUTH_REQUIRED=yes DEBUG=no ALLOWED_HOSTS="*" PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 APPRISE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/container/config APPRISE_STORAGE_DIR=/home/container/config/store APPRISE_ATTACH_DIR=/home/container/attach APPRISE_PLUGIN_PATHS=/home/container/plugin; cd app && exec ../.venv/bin/gunicorn -c gunicorn.conf.py --pythonpath /home/container/app --bind 0.0.0.0:{{SERVER_PORT}} --workers {{APPRISE_WORKER_COUNT}} --worker-tmp-dir /tmp --log-level info raptor_wsgi:application

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Apprise API: downloads the chosen Apprise API release's source from GitHub
# into app/, and makes the server's own secret key once. Its Python packages
# are installed when the server starts, for the Python version it runs.
# The saved configurations (config/), attachments, plugins and the secret
# key are never touched; app/ is only replaced once the new one is unpacked.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$want" = latest ] || want="v${want#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag caronc/apprise-api "$want") || fail "Apprise API has no version ${VERSION:-latest}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 2.1.0, then reinstall."

if [ -f app/manage.py ] && [ "$(cat .apprise-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Apprise API $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Apprise API $tag"
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$work/src.tar.gz" "https://github.com/caronc/apprise-api/archive/refs/tags/$tag.tar.gz" ||
        fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    tar -xzf "$work/src.tar.gz" -C "$work" --strip-components=1
    [ -f "$work/apprise_api/manage.py" ] && [ -f "$work/requirements.txt" ] || fail "The download isn't Apprise API's source. Reinstall to try again."
    cp "$work/requirements.txt" "$work/apprise_api/requirements.txt"
    rm -rf app.old
    [ ! -d app ] || mv app app.old
    mv "$work/apprise_api" app
    rm -rf app.old
    echo "$tag" > .apprise-version
fi

# The release runs behind nginx, which serves its static files; here
# gunicorn serves them itself, through WhiteNoise.
cat > app/raptor_wsgi.py <<'PY'
# Written by Raptor's install: Apprise API with its static files served by
# WhiteNoise instead of nginx.
import os
from core.wsgi import application as app
from whitenoise import WhiteNoise

application = WhiteNoise(app, root=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "static"), prefix="s/")
PY

mkdir -p config/store attach plugin
# Django's secret key (it also names saved configurations), made here once.
if [ ! -s .secret-key ]; then
    head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '\n' > .secret-key
    chmod 600 .secret-key
fi
echo "Installed Apprise API $tag (its Python packages are installed when the server starts)."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Apprise API version to install, such as 2.1.0, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Admin username
variables.description: The username for the web interface and API.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The password for the web interface and API. Leave it empty to use a random one, saved in admin-password.txt.

variables.name: Workers
variables.description: How many web worker processes to run.
